key_features.classic_presentation: ONSET: CHRONIC, RECURRENT pattern over months to years (NOT acute). Gradual development, waxing and waning. LOCATION: LOWER ABDOMEN, diffuse. Cramping migrates, not fixed to one spot. DURATION: CHRONIC condition lasting months to years. Individual cramping episodes last minutes to hours. Symptoms present at least once per week for 3+ months. CHARACTER: CRAMPY, INTERMITTENT discomfort. NOT sharp or severe. Bloating, gas sensations. AGGRAVATING: STRESS worsens symptoms significantly. Certain FOODS trigger (dairy, gluten, FODMAPs). Anxiety increases cramping. RELIEVING: DEFECATION provides relief. Stress reduction helps. Dietary changes improve. Antispasmodics reduce cramping. TIMING: INTERMITTENT cramping related to bowel movements. Pattern waxes and wanes. Often worse with stress. NO NOCTURNAL symptoms (doesn't wake from sleep). SEVERITY: 3-6/10, mild to moderate. Not severe enough to disrupt daily life significantly. ASSOCIATED SYMPTOMS: BLOATING and gas, mucus in stool (NO blood), sense of incomplete evacuation, alternating diarrhea/constipation. KEY POSITIVES: Chronic >6 months, pain relief with defecation, stress/food triggers, NO alarm features (no blood, weight loss, fever). KEY NEGATIVES: NEW onset age >50 needs workup for cancer. BLOOD in stool rules out irritable bowel syndrome (IBS). Weight loss, fever, NOCTURNAL diarrhea suggests inflammatory bowel disease (IBD)/organic disease.

red_flags: Blood in stool - needs colonoscopy to rule out inflammatory bowel disease (IBD) or colon cancer
Unintentional weight loss - organic pathology, not irritable bowel syndrome (IBS)
New onset after age 50 - higher risk of colon cancer, needs colonoscopy
Nocturnal symptoms waking patient from sleep - suggests organic disease
